ground_truth.description: The refactor silently changes FakeScheduler's cache semantics. Previously `_status_cache` was an empty dict that `set_task_status` never populated, so the workflow's `cached in TERMINAL_STATUSES` check always saw `None` and re-queued. The new `get_cached_status` returns `history[-1]` (the actual last status), so if the last status is terminal the workflow now takes the 'not re-queueing' branch. This is a behavioral divergence in a refactor claimed to be behavior-preserving, and can alter which code path e2e tests exercise.

The added `assert result is not None` is redundant — an identical assertion already exists three lines earlier (line 681) and no code between them reassigns `result`. It adds nothing and is dead/duplicated code.
`from typing import TYPE_CHECKING` is added but there is no visible usage in the diff; if nothing in the file references it, this is an unused import that will trip linters.

The only production consumer of the new `get_cached_status` seam, the post-steward terminal guard in TaskWorkflow (returns DONE for cached 'done', BLOCKED for other terminal statuses, without re-queueing to pending), is exercised by no test; the new tests only check each double's getter echoes its setter, so a regression in the guard (wrong accessor, wrong task id, mishandled 'cancelled') would pass.

_EvalScheduler's status map is renamed from `_status_cache` to the less informative `_cache` for no reason (the Protocol no longer exposes it), so it no longer says what it holds and no longer matches `Scheduler._status_cache`, which stores the same concept.

The change adds an 11-line banner above the TYPE_CHECKING block defending its placement against a rejected alternative and citing FakeScheduler by line ('line ~361', the class is at 350), a second banner near 2026 narrating history ('replaced the old hasattr/isinstance runtime checks'), and 'Uses get_cached_status() to verify cache contents.' sentences in TestGetTasksSeedsCache/TestCancelledTaskResync docstrings; reviewer-answering and change-history prose plus a drifting line pin, where a one-line pointer suffices.

The TestEvalSchedulerCachedStatus tests import OrchestratorConfig inside each function although the module already imports it at top level (line 21), and import _EvalScheduler separately in each test and again under an alias in the TYPE_CHECKING block.

TestGetCachedStatus.test_get_cached_status_returns_status_after_set_task_status repeats the set_task_status-then-get_cached_status check that TestGetTasksSeedsCache and TestCancelledTaskResync now already make via the new accessor; only the None-for-unknown case adds coverage.
Unit tests of the eval stub `_EvalScheduler` (evals/runner.py) are added to the workflow e2e test module instead of an evals-focused module, mixing concerns in that file.

task.description:
Two improvements to _SchedulerLike Protocol in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py:
1. Replace _status_cache dict attribute with get_cached_status(task_id) method. Update all three implementors (Scheduler, FakeScheduler, _EvalScheduler) and the call site at workflow.py:1884.
2. Replace runtime hasattr/isinstance conformance tests in test_workflow_e2e.py with static TYPE_CHECKING assertions that catch method signature drift.
